title: Rendering A* Open/Closed Set Snapshots and the Final Path
description: Define draw_state to encode free cells, walls, closed_set, open_set, and path as grayscale intensities in img, then plot four search snapshots and the final path.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: In `draw_state`, initialize `img` with separate supplied intensities for free cells and walls (`grid == 1`). Assign the respective intensities to `closed_set`, `open_set` cells outside `closed_set`, and cells on `path`.
Display `img` with `plt.imshow(img, interpolation='nearest')` and overlay markers for `start` (`'o'`), `goal` (`'x'`), and `current` (`'s'`).
Notice the intensity hierarchy in `img`: unvisited free cells, frontier cells in `open_set`, expanded cells in `closed_set`, the final `path`, and walls have distinct intensities.

steps.question: If a cell `(i, j)` appears in both `open_set` and `closed_set` during a snapshot, what intensity value does `img[i, j]` end up with after lines 8-14?
steps.answer: It keeps the closed-set intensity. Line 10 sets that intensity for `(i, j)` in `closed_set`, and the open-set update checks `(i, j) not in closed_set` before overwriting.

steps.description: Extract `snaps = RES["snapshots"]` and call `draw_state` at four indices: the first, one-third, two-thirds, and last snapshot indices. Call `draw_state` once more on line 38 with `path=path`.
